Annotation Interface TypeHierarchyImport

@Documented @Retention(CLASS) @Target(TYPE) public @interface TypeHierarchyImport
Imports the generic hierarchy of a type into the compilation, as a record the compiler writes, to be found at run time with TypeHierarchies.find(Class) as a TypeHierarchy. Like Introspected.classes(), it can import the hierarchies of classes that cannot be annotated.

Put on a class without classes(), it imports the hierarchy of that class. With classes(), it imports the hierarchies of those classes instead, which can be classes of a library or of the JDK, such as the class of a value an application passes where its generic supertypes are needed at run time:

@TypeHierarchyImport(classes = {ArrayList.class, HashMap.class})
class Hierarchies {
}

A record is a small generated class, one per type, loaded only when the type is asked for. It carries the type variables with their bounds, the generic superclass and the generic interfaces as the type declares them, and nothing of its members.

Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

    • classes

      Class<?>[] classes
      The classes to import the hierarchies of, instead of the annotated class. When none is given, the default, the hierarchy of the annotated class itself is imported, and the annotated class can be the type whose hierarchy a consumer asks for at run time.
      Returns:
      The classes, empty for the annotated class
      Default:
      {}
